questions.stem: An Oregon applicant completed Basics seven months before applying. What needs attention?
options: Ask an employer to waive it
Complete timely approved education
Keep the old education indefinitely
Buy a stamp first
questions.explanation: Education must fall within six months before application.
feedback: An employer cannot waive state qualifications.
Correct. Education must fall within six months before application.
Training has a six-month window.
Equipment does not refresh education.

questions.stem: A teenager turns eighteen next month and wants an Oregon appointment today. Which qualification prevents appointment now?
options: The minimum age of eighteen
A five-year residency rule
A mandatory bond
A college degree
questions.explanation: Oregon requires the applicant to be at least eighteen.
feedback: Correct. Oregon requires the applicant to be at least eighteen.
That is not the stated age requirement.
Oregon does not mandate a bond.
The qualification list does not require a degree.

questions.stem: An Oregon resident cannot read or write English and asks a coworker to manage every notarization. Which qualification remains unmet?
options: Ownership of an office
Membership in a trade association
Purchase of insurance
Ability to read and write English
questions.explanation: The applicant personally must meet the English-language qualification.
feedback: Office ownership is not this qualification.
Membership does not supply language ability.
Insurance cannot replace personal qualifications.
Correct. The applicant personally must meet the English-language qualification.

questions.stem: An applicant discloses a notary revocation from four years ago. What Oregon screening issue arises?
options: Revocation never matters after resignation
Only unpaid fees are reviewed
Revocation within the preceding ten years
Only Oregon work experience counts
questions.explanation: Oregon screens applicants for a revocation in the ten-year period.
feedback: Resignation does not remove the listed disqualification.
Background and revocation history are reviewed.
Correct. Oregon screens applicants for a revocation in the ten-year period.
Experience does not erase revocation history.

questions.stem: A recent fraud conviction appears in an Oregon applicant's history. Which claim would conflict with the qualifications?
options: Review the current qualifications
A fraud conviction is irrelevant to commissioning
The application undergoes screening
Disclose accurate application information
questions.explanation: The qualifications address crimes involving fraud, dishonesty or deceit within ten years.
feedback: The official list identifies disqualifications.
Correct. The qualifications address crimes involving fraud, dishonesty or deceit within ten years.
Background screening is part of the process.
Accurate disclosure is necessary.

questions.stem: A training vendor says its completion paper authorizes Oregon notarizations while the application is pending. Which document actually establishes the appointment?
options: The state commission certificate
The vendor's sales receipt
The course attendance list
The employer's job offer
questions.explanation: Training completion does not itself confer notarial authority.
feedback: Correct. Training completion does not itself confer notarial authority.
A receipt establishes purchase, not appointment.
Attendance alone does not commission anyone.
An employer cannot issue an Oregon commission.

questions.stem: An applicant loses the emailed Oregon oath and wants to recreate its application section from memory. What does the guide direct?
options: Rewrite the section freely
Replace the oath with an invoice
Have a stamp vendor issue the oath
Use the state's form without changing its application section
questions.explanation: The guide directs applicants not to change the application section of the emailed form.
feedback: The state's completed application section is not to be changed.
An invoice does not satisfy the oath.
The commissioning office supplies that document.
Correct. The guide directs applicants not to change the application section of the emailed form.

questions.stem: An Oregon oath has been sitting unsigned for forty days after issuance. What consequence does the guide identify?
options: Begin work while it is pending
Extend the deadline on the form
Take the test again to obtain a new oath
Send the stale oath whenever convenient
questions.explanation: The guide requires submission within thirty days of issuance and describes retesting after a missed deadline.
feedback: An unfinished oath process does not activate authority.
The applicant cannot grant an extension.
Correct. The guide requires submission within thirty days of issuance and describes retesting after a missed deadline.
The stated oath deadline has passed.

questions.stem: An Oregon stamp maker asks for the Certificate of Authorization. What is its purpose?
options: Authorize the vendor to notarize
Verify the information for making the official stamp
Prove the customer owns real estate
Replace the notarial certificate on every document
questions.explanation: The authorization certificate supplies the commissioned name, number and expiration.
feedback: The vendor does not acquire the applicant's authority.
Correct. The authorization certificate supplies the commissioned name, number and expiration.
It concerns the notary's commission.
It is a supply authorization document.

questions.stem: An Oregon supplier offers to manufacture a commission stamp without reviewing any authorization. What does the guide recommend?
options: Choose a vendor that requires the authorization certificate
Send only a business card
Let the supplier invent a commission number
Use the supplier's sample expiration
questions.explanation: The guide warns against vendors that omit this verification.
feedback: Correct. The guide warns against vendors that omit this verification.
A business card does not verify commission details.
The state issues the number.
The stamp needs the actual commission information.

questions.stem: An Oregon applicant has two middle names but applies using middle initials alone. What name should the commission normally show?
options: Only an office nickname
The employer's business name
Any shortened name used online
The full legal name including middle names
questions.explanation: The Oregon guide requires the full legal first, middle and last names.
feedback: A nickname is not the normal commissioned name.
A business is not the commissioned individual.
An online profile does not establish the legal name.
Correct. The Oregon guide requires the full legal first, middle and last names.

questions.stem: An Oregon applicant's ID supports a full commissioned name and a shorter customary signature. Must the handwritten signature reproduce every printed name?
options: Only an employer may approve the signature
The signature may be unverified
No, an ID-verified legal signature may differ in form
Yes, every letter must match the printed name
questions.explanation: The commissioned name and verified commission signature serve different functions.
feedback: Identity evidence controls the signature verification.
The guide requires ID verification.
Correct. The commissioned name and verified commission signature serve different functions.
The guide allows an ID-verified signature form.

questions.stem: A Salem notary assumes a reminder letter will arrive before the term ends. What should the notary do?
options: Ask the stamp seller to renew it
Track expiration and reapply independently
Continue until a reminder arrives
Keep the same commission forever
questions.explanation: The guide says the commission is not automatically renewed and reminders are not sent.
feedback: Only the state handles commissioning.
Correct. The guide says the commission is not automatically renewed and reminders are not sent.
Lack of a reminder does not extend authority.
Each term requires a new commission.

questions.stem: A notary wants to file the next Oregon application two months before expiration. What filing window does the guide give?
options: The thirty days before expiration
Any time in the final year
Only after a one-year lapse
The day after the next election
questions.explanation: The guide permits a new application thirty days before the current term expires.
feedback: Correct. The guide permits a new application thirty days before the current term expires.
That exceeds the stated window.
A lapse is not required.
Elections do not determine the window.

questions.stem: A renewed Oregon notary notices that the new commission has a different number. Is the old number automatically carried forward?
options: Yes, the state must preserve the old number
The employer chooses which number to use
The old and new numbers should be combined
No, each new commission has its own number and expiration
questions.explanation: The guide describes each commission as unique.
feedback: The guide says a new number is issued.
The state-issued commission controls.
Combining numbers misstates the commission.
Correct. The guide describes each commission as unique.

questions.stem: A new Oregon term begins while many pages remain in the existing journal. What permits continued use?
options: Leave the expired term information unchanged
Share remaining pages with another notary
Update the front information and mark where the new term begins
Destroy all earlier entries
questions.explanation: The guide allows continued use with updated commission information.
feedback: The front information must be current.
Notaries must maintain separate journals.
Correct. The guide allows continued use with updated commission information.
Existing entries remain subject to retention.

questions.stem: An Oregon commission expires tonight and a replacement appointment is still pending. How should the old stamp be handled?
options: Lend it to an active colleague
Disable it when the old commission expires
Use it until the replacement arrives
Alter the expiration with a pen
questions.explanation: An expired stamp must be rendered unusable under the guide.
feedback: Another person cannot use that stamp.
Correct. An expired stamp must be rendered unusable under the guide.
Pending reapplication does not extend the old term.
Handwriting does not create a new authorized stamp.

questions.stem: A misplaced Oregon stamp is recovered after the state issued replacement authorization. What does the guide require concerning the original?
options: Report its recovery in writing and destroy it
Keep both as interchangeable stamps
Give it to the former employer
Erase the notary's name and sell it
questions.explanation: The guide requires a written explanation within ten days and destruction of the recovered stamp.
feedback: Correct. The guide requires a written explanation within ten days and destruction of the recovered stamp.
The recovered original must be destroyed.
The employer cannot use the original.
The guide directs destruction, not resale.

questions.stem: An Oregon journal is destroyed by a burst water pipe. What official process should the notary use?
options: Quietly reconstruct signatures
Throw away every related record
Use a coworker's journal permanently
Report the unusable journal through the prescribed state form
questions.explanation: The guide provides a missing or unusable journal reporting process.
feedback: Reconstruction cannot replace actual signer signatures.
Records should be handled through the state process.
Each notary needs an individual journal.
Correct. The guide provides a missing or unusable journal reporting process.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary moves to a different mailing address during the term. What obligation continues?
options: Change only the stamp vendor's address
Ask customers to forward official notices
Update commission contact information with the state
Wait until an investigation begins
questions.explanation: The guide requires current commission information.
feedback: Vendor records do not update the state.
That does not update the commission record.
Correct. The guide requires current commission information.
Updating is an ongoing duty.

questions.stem: A bank limits employee notarizations during working hours to account holders. Which condition does the guide emphasize?
options: Every refusal is automatically lawful
The access policy must avoid unlawful discrimination
The policy allows false certificates
The bank owns the employees' commissions
questions.explanation: Employers may limit workplace access while observing protected-class restrictions.
feedback: Access restrictions still need lawful implementation.
Correct. Employers may limit workplace access while observing protected-class restrictions.
Access limits do not excuse false certification.
Commissions belong to individuals.

questions.stem: An employer orders an Oregon notary never to notarize on personal time away from work. What does the guide say?
options: An employer cannot impose that off-premises personal-time prohibition
The order transfers the commission to the employer
The order changes state boundaries
The order replaces all state rules
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes workplace scheduling from a notary's own time away.
feedback: Correct. The guide distinguishes workplace scheduling from a notary's own time away.
Employment does not transfer a commission.
Workplace policies do not change jurisdiction.
State notarial duties continue.

questions.stem: A manager threatens dismissal unless an Oregon employee notarizes an absent client's signature. What should the employee do?
options: Follow the order because the employer accepts liability
Backdate the certificate to the client's visit
Let the manager use the stamp
Require lawful appearance and decline the improper request
questions.explanation: Employer pressure does not authorize notarial misconduct.
feedback: Liability arrangements do not authorize the act.
The notary cannot certify an act that did not occur.
The manager cannot exercise the employee's authority.
Correct. Employer pressure does not authorize notarial misconduct.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary deliberately omits the signer from the procedure to keep a sale moving. How does the guide characterize deliberate disobedience of a notarial rule?
options: An automatic education exemption
A private business custom that overrides law
Intentional misconduct
A harmless customer preference
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes deliberate disobedience from negligent errors.
feedback: Misconduct creates no exemption.
Business custom cannot displace notarial duties.
Correct. The guide distinguishes deliberate disobedience from negligent errors.
Appearance is a required safeguard.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary accidentally leaves the county blank on a certificate. Is an accidental error automatically outside misconduct rules?
options: Yes, if no fee was charged
No, negligent or accidental improper notarization can be misconduct
Yes, only criminal fraud counts
Yes, if the document is accepted
questions.explanation: The guide includes unintentional misconduct.
feedback: Unpaid service still requires proper certification.
Correct. The guide includes unintentional misconduct.
Administrative and civil issues can arise without criminal fraud.
Acceptance does not cure the omission.

questions.stem: A notary buys E&O insurance and assumes Oregon places a fixed ceiling on all resulting civil liability. What is the guide's warning?
options: Policy limits do not cap the notary's possible liability
Insurance eliminates every lawsuit
A bond always pays unlimited damages
Insurance authorizes intentional false statements
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes limited insurance coverage from potentially larger civil damages.
feedback: Correct. The guide distinguishes limited insurance coverage from potentially larger civil damages.
Coverage does not prevent claims.
Bond payouts also have limits.
Insurance never authorizes misconduct.

questions.stem: A nonattorney Oregon notary advertises as a notario publico to attract immigration clients. What change is required?
options: Add a larger seal image
Charge only a small fee
Advertise only on social media
Stop using the prohibited title
questions.explanation: Oregon restricts nonattorney use of notario or notario publico.
feedback: An image does not cure a prohibited title.
The title restriction is not based on price.
Online advertising is still covered.
Correct. Oregon restricts nonattorney use of notario or notario publico.

questions.stem: A nonattorney Oregon notary's website offers paid advice about which immigration petition to submit. What should the notary remove?
options: The official contact address
All truthful descriptions of authorized acts
The offer of legal advice beyond notarial authority
The required legal-services disclaimer
questions.explanation: A notarial commission does not authorize immigration legal advice.
feedback: Removing contact information does not resolve the legal-advice issue.
Authorized services may be described truthfully.
Correct. A notarial commission does not authorize immigration legal advice.
The disclaimer remains required in advertising.

questions.stem: An Oregon nonattorney notary runs a radio advertisement. Does the advertising warning apply to broadcast media?
options: Only when the listener requests legal advice
Yes, the warning applies across advertising media
No, warnings apply only to signs
No, spoken advertisements are exempt
questions.explanation: The guide includes broadcast, internet and print advertising.
feedback: The warning is an advertising requirement.
Correct. The guide includes broadcast, internet and print advertising.
Broadcast advertisements are included.
The guide creates no spoken-ad exception.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary posts an advertisement in Spanish. In what language should the required legal-services warning appear?
options: The language of the advertisement
English only regardless of the ad
Any language chosen by the employer
No warning if a price appears
questions.explanation: The guide requires the warning in the ad's language.
feedback: Correct. The guide requires the warning in the ad's language.
That would not satisfy the stated language instruction.
The ad's language controls.
A price does not waive the warning.

questions.stem: An Oregon employer asks a notary to complete Form I-9 as its authorized representative. How should the capacity be understood?
options: An acknowledgment of federal employment
A copy certification of citizenship
A mandatory jurat for every employee
An employer-representative task without a notarial stamp
questions.explanation: The guide identifies I-9 verification as a nonnotarial function.
feedback: The form has no notarial certificate for that act.
That misstates the I-9 task.
The guide does not classify it as a jurat.
Correct. The guide identifies I-9 verification as a nonnotarial function.

questions.stem: A stock-transfer customer asks an Oregon notary for a Medallion Signature Guarantee. What should the notary explain?
options: Any notary may sell one as a jurat
The journal signature guarantees the securities
That guarantee is a financial-institution service
The official stamp supplies the guarantee
questions.explanation: A Medallion guarantee is distinct from an Oregon notarial service.
feedback: A jurat does not supply the guarantee.
A journal entry does not guarantee a transfer.
Correct. A Medallion guarantee is distinct from an Oregon notarial service.
A notarial stamp does not create a Medallion guarantee.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary wishes to charge less than the ordinary maximum for all low-income customers under a consistent policy. What does the guide permit?
options: A higher fee based on protected status
A consistently applied lawful reduced-fee policy
An absolute duty to charge the maximum
Unlimited charges to other customers
questions.explanation: The guide permits reductions or waivers applied consistently without bias.
feedback: Fees must be consistent and nonbiased.
Correct. The guide permits reductions or waivers applied consistently without bias.
The maximum is a ceiling.
Other fees remain subject to the cap.

questions.stem: An Oregon mobile notary discloses a travel charge only after arriving. What should have happened?
options: Agree on the travel fee before the meeting
Hide travel in the state act fee
Call it a tax to avoid agreement
Let the customer learn it from the invoice afterward
questions.explanation: Travel charges are separate and must be agreed in advance.
feedback: Correct. Travel charges are separate and must be agreed in advance.
Separate travel must be disclosed.
Relabeling does not remove the requirement.
Post-service disclosure is too late.

questions.stem: Two signers acknowledge signatures in one Oregon paper certificate. What fee principle applies?
options: One page always means one act
The fee equals the property's value
The second signer is automatically free
Each separately notarized signature represents an act
questions.explanation: The guide's example allows separate ordinary-act fees for two signatures.
feedback: The guide counts the separate signatures.
Property value is not the fee unit.
A shared certificate does not require a free second act.
Correct. The guide's example allows separate ordinary-act fees for two signatures.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary has never filed a fee waiver but wants to perform a free notarization. May the notary waive that particular fee?
options: Only the state may waive a customer's fee
Only a lawyer may provide free acts
Yes, charging is optional absent another restriction
No, the maximum is mandatory
questions.explanation: Not filing a waiver does not create a duty to charge.
feedback: The guide permits a notary to waive fees.
The guide imposes no lawyer-only limit.
Correct. Not filing a waiver does not create a duty to charge.
The maximum does not compel a charge.

questions.stem: A notary's Oregon fee waiver is still on file. A neighbor requests an after-hours paid act. What controls?
options: The waiver applies only to the old employer
The filed waiver also applies after hours
After-hours work automatically cancels the waiver
A neighbor may orally override the waiver
questions.explanation: The waiver follows the notary's acts until properly rescinded.
feedback: The waiver concerns the notary's charging right.
Correct. The waiver follows the notary's acts until properly rescinded.
Time of day does not rescind it.
A customer cannot cancel the filed statement.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary wants to resume charging after filing a fee waiver. What state action does the guide describe?
options: Rescind the waiver through written notice or the online change process
Discard the personal copy of the waiver
Charge one customer to cancel it
Ask a coworker to announce the change
questions.explanation: The guide identifies state notice to resume charging.
feedback: Correct. The guide identifies state notice to resume charging.
Destroying a copy does not rescind the filing.
Charging does not cancel the state record.
A coworker's announcement does not update the filing.

questions.stem: A private Oregon employer collects employees' notarial fees. Does that arrangement permit exceeding the state act maximum?
options: Yes, business invoices are unlimited
Yes, if payroll keeps the money
Only if the client pays by card
No, the statutory maximum still governs
questions.explanation: An employer-fee arrangement cannot enlarge permissible notarial charges.
feedback: The act fee remains regulated.
Recipient of revenue does not alter the cap.
Payment method does not change the maximum.
Correct. An employer-fee arrangement cannot enlarge permissible notarial charges.

questions.stem: A shop displays only a sign saying Notary Available and reveals its act fee after notarization. What must change?
options: Announce the price only if challenged
Add the price only to the journal
Display or provide the fee schedule beforehand
Use a larger stamp
questions.explanation: Customers must have advance notice and the chance to decline the price.
feedback: Advance disclosure is required.
The private record does not inform the customer beforehand.
Correct. Customers must have advance notice and the chance to decline the price.
Stamp size does not disclose fees.

questions.stem: A regular coffee-shop customer asks an Oregon notary to rely on seeing him occasionally. What must personal knowledge provide?
options: Payment before identification
Reasonable certainty from a meaningful prior relationship
Recognition of his coffee order
An employer's unsupported introduction
questions.explanation: A nodding acquaintance alone does not meet the guide's personal-knowledge standard.
feedback: Payment supplies no identity evidence.
Correct. A nodding acquaintance alone does not meet the guide's personal-knowledge standard.
Ordering habits alone do not establish identity.
An introduction is not the notary's personal knowledge.

questions.stem: An Oregon signer brings a credible witness whom the notary has never met. Must that alone defeat the witness route?
options: No, identify the witness through an approved credential
Yes, all credible witnesses must be childhood friends
No identification of the witness is needed
The witness may identify herself by telephone
questions.explanation: The notary may know the witness personally or establish the witness's identity satisfactorily.
feedback: Correct. The notary may know the witness personally or establish the witness's identity satisfactorily.
The guide permits documentary identification.
The witness must be identified.
Required appearance is not replaced by a call.

questions.stem: An Oregon witness knows the notary well but has never met the signer. Which necessary connection is missing?
options: The notary's knowledge of the document's author
The witness's ownership of a stamp
The signer's employment by the notary
The witness's personal knowledge of the signer
questions.explanation: A credible witness must personally know the person being identified.
feedback: That is not this identity connection.
The witness need not be a notary.
Employment is not required.
Correct. A credible witness must personally know the person being identified.

questions.stem: At a paper signing, an Oregon credible witness offers an unsworn note identifying the signer. What additional procedure is required?
options: Staple the note to the ID
Have the witness text the recipient
Administer the witness's oath or affirmation
Collect a second customer fee
questions.explanation: The witness must give sworn or affirmed identity testimony.
feedback: Attachment does not replace the oath.
Recipient correspondence does not complete the procedure.
Correct. The witness must give sworn or affirmed identity testimony.
An extra fee does not create sworn testimony.

questions.stem: A witness who is a party to an Oregon transaction volunteers to vouch for an unfamiliar signer. What concern does the guide identify?
options: The witness can replace the absent principal
The witness must be impartial and lack transaction interest
A party is always the best identity witness
Signing twice removes the conflict
questions.explanation: The guide's witness procedure screens financial interest and party status.
feedback: The signer must also participate.
Correct. The guide's witness procedure screens financial interest and party status.
Interest undermines the required impartial role.
An additional signature does not remove interest.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary uses a credible witness to identify an acknowledgment signer. How does the guide document the two people?
options: Record the witness and the signer's act in the described entries
Record only the witness's first name
Record only the document recipient
Skip all entries because a witness attended
questions.explanation: The guide calls for witness information and a separate signer-act entry.
feedback: Correct. The guide calls for witness information and a separate signer-act entry.
That omits required identification detail.
The recipient did not supply the sworn identification.
Witness use does not remove journaling.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary wants an extra act fee merely for administering the credible witness's identity oath. What does the guide explain?
options: Charge the RON maximum
Double the acknowledgment fee automatically
Charge based on the witness's distance traveled
That identity oath is part of verification and has no separate fee
questions.explanation: The guide expressly treats it as part of identifying the signer.
feedback: A paper identity oath is not a RON fee category.
The witness oath is not separately charged.
Travel does not create an extra witness-oath act fee.
Correct. The guide expressly treats it as part of identifying the signer.

questions.stem: An Oregon customer offers an otherwise qualifying government photo-and-signature ID expired two years ago. Which timing rule applies?
options: Ten expired years are always permitted
Expiration is irrelevant to every credential
It may fit the three-year expiration allowance
Every expired ID is prohibited
questions.explanation: The guide permits the listed IDs current or expired no more than three years.
feedback: The ordinary allowance is three years.
The listed timing condition still applies.
Correct. The guide permits the listed IDs current or expired no more than three years.
The guide permits a limited expiration period.

questions.stem: An Oregon signer offers only a U.S. passport card. Why does the guide reject that card by itself?
options: Only Oregon-issued passports qualify
It lacks the required signature
It was issued by the wrong country
Its color is not blue
questions.explanation: The guide requires both photograph and signature for this documentary route.
feedback: Oregon does not issue passports.
Correct. The guide requires both photograph and signature for this documentary route.
A U.S. issuer is not the identified problem.
Color is not the stated test.

questions.stem: A valid foreign passport recognized by the United States shows the Oregon signer's photograph and signature. Is foreign issuance alone disqualifying?
options: No, an officially recognized foreign passport is listed
Yes, only U.S. citizens may sign
Yes, all IDs must be issued in Oregon
No, so all private travel cards qualify too
questions.explanation: The guide includes officially recognized passports of foreign countries.
feedback: Correct. The guide includes officially recognized passports of foreign countries.
Citizenship is not that documentary limitation.
The approved categories are broader.
Recognition of passports does not approve private cards.

questions.stem: A federally recognized tribe's permanent ID has the signer's photo and signature but no expiration date. How does the Oregon guide address it?
options: Invent an expiration date
Treat every tribal ID as counterfeit
Add an expiration date to the card
It may be considered permanent
questions.explanation: The guide recognizes that some qualifying tribal IDs lack expiration dates.
feedback: The notary must not invent credential information.
The guide recognizes the qualifying category.
The notary cannot alter the issuer's credential.
Correct. The guide recognizes that some qualifying tribal IDs lack expiration dates.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary sees a military ID containing a photo but no signature. What issue remains?
options: The customer must buy a state bond
The missing signature can be supplied on the card by the notary
It lacks a required feature for the ordinary documentary route
Military service automatically proves every name
questions.explanation: The guide limits military ID use to cards containing photograph and signature.
feedback: A bond does not supply identity evidence.
The notary cannot create an issuer credential feature.
Correct. The guide limits military ID use to cards containing photograph and signature.
Service does not waive the stated credential features.

questions.stem: An Oregon prisoner needs a notarization. Which identity route does the guide identify for the facility setting?
options: No incarcerated person may ever obtain a notarization
Facility identification established through official government records
Any nickname used by another inmate
The case number by itself always suffices
questions.explanation: The guide addresses correctional identification based on official records and comparison.
feedback: The guide provides a correctional-facility route.
Correct. The guide addresses correctional identification based on official records and comparison.
A nickname is not the official identification route.
A case number alone is not the described identification.

questions.stem: A customer's Oregon license is damaged so badly that the face cannot be compared. What may the notary request?
options: Additional identification information or credentials
A larger fee instead of identification
Only a promise to return tomorrow
A blank certificate signed in advance
questions.explanation: The guide permits additional evidence when identity remains uncertain.
feedback: Correct. The guide permits additional evidence when identity remains uncertain.
Money does not resolve identity.
A promise is not present identity evidence.
An incomplete certificate does not resolve identity.

questions.stem: An Oregon customer presents only a matricula consular card for the primary identity check. What does the guide say?
options: It automatically replaces every passport
It proves representative authority
It eliminates personal appearance
It is insufficient by itself under Oregon's listed routes
questions.explanation: The guide permits it only as backup information, not the sole qualifying credential.
feedback: The guide does not list it as an independent substitute.
An identity card does not prove agency powers.
No card eliminates required participation.
Correct. The guide permits it only as backup information, not the sole qualifying credential.

questions.stem: A seventeen-year-old Oregon signer brings acceptable ID and understands a document. Does minority automatically prohibit notarization?
options: No, so skip the ID check
Only if a parent signs for the child without direction
No, assess identity, willingness and capacity
Yes, all signers must be eighteen
questions.explanation: The guide permits minors with appropriate safeguards.
feedback: Minors still need acceptable identification.
A parent cannot automatically replace the actual signer.
Correct. The guide permits minors with appropriate safeguards.
The guide distinguishes signer age from notary eligibility.

questions.stem: A hospital signer is too disoriented to describe the document despite prompting. What should the Oregon notary do?
options: Assume a hospital admission proves capacity
Decline while capacity remains unresolved
Rely entirely on a visitor's urgency
Stamp first and interview later
questions.explanation: The guide directs caution and refusal when sufficient awareness cannot be established.
feedback: Admission supplies no such presumption.
Correct. The guide directs caution and refusal when sufficient awareness cannot be established.
Urgency does not establish capacity.
Capacity is assessed before completion.

questions.stem: An Oregon caregiver answers every question and prevents the signer from speaking. What is the appropriate next step?
options: Speak directly with the signer to assess willingness and awareness
Accept the caregiver's answers as the signer's oath
Ask only whether the caregiver paid
Finish before the caregiver becomes impatient
questions.explanation: The guide advises controlling the procedure and assessing the signer personally.
feedback: Correct. The guide advises controlling the procedure and assessing the signer personally.
Another person cannot make the signer's oath.
Payment does not resolve coercion.
Pressure is a reason for scrutiny.

questions.stem: An Oregon borrower wants a signature notarized on a form with substantive blanks to be filled tomorrow. What should happen?
options: Stamp across the empty spaces
Authorize the lender to fill the certificate later
Charge more to compensate for risk
Resolve the incomplete-document issue before notarization
questions.explanation: The guide warns against notarizing blank or incomplete documents.
feedback: A stamp does not resolve missing terms.
The notary must complete an accurate certificate.
Fees do not authorize incomplete-document notarization.
Correct. The guide warns against notarizing blank or incomplete documents.

questions.stem: A customer says some form fields are intentionally inapplicable. Who should indicate that intention in the document?
options: The notary should sign for every absent party
The recipient's future silence supplies the missing entries
The customer should mark the intended blanks appropriately
The notary should invent substantive answers
questions.explanation: The guide gives N/A as an example for intended blanks.
feedback: Absent parties cannot be manufactured.
Future silence does not complete the document.
Correct. The guide gives N/A as an example for intended blanks.
That risks unauthorized document preparation.

questions.stem: A deed signer appears before an Oregon notary but says the signature belongs to someone else. Can that signer acknowledge it as their own?
options: Yes, after adding a witness
No, the acknowledgment must concern that person's signature
Yes, if the signer owns similar property
Yes, if the notary recognizes the handwriting
questions.explanation: The notary must identify the actual signer and take the required acknowledgment.
feedback: A witness cannot turn another person's signature into this signer's.
Correct. The notary must identify the actual signer and take the required acknowledgment.
Property similarity does not establish execution.
Recognition does not replace the actual person's acknowledgment.

questions.stem: An Oregon client plans to sign a document next week but wants its acknowledgment completed today. What prevents completion?
options: The signature cannot be made after the acknowledgment
Only the page count
A missing travel receipt
The customer's county of residence
questions.explanation: The guide permits earlier signing but does not permit a future signature.
feedback: Correct. The guide permits earlier signing but does not permit a future signature.
Page count does not cure future execution.
Travel billing does not determine the act.
Residence does not fix the absent signature.

questions.stem: A corporation's officer acknowledges a contract in Oregon. Which execution fact belongs to the representative acknowledgment?
options: The corporation physically appeared
The notary guarantees the corporation's debts
The officer must swear to all business accounts
The officer acted with authority for the identified entity
questions.explanation: Representative acknowledgment includes the proper authority and represented person's act.
feedback: A corporation acts through its authorized individual.
The notary makes no debt guarantee.
That is not the acknowledgment procedure.
Correct. Representative acknowledgment includes the proper authority and represented person's act.

questions.stem: An Oregon agent signs under a power of attorney. What does the guide recommend regarding representative capacity?
options: Always certify the agent owns the principal's property
Skip the agent's identity because a power exists
Review suitable confirmation of that capacity
Treat the notary's commission as the power of attorney
questions.explanation: The guide describes supporting authority review as best practice.
feedback: Representation does not imply ownership.
The appearing agent must still be identified.
Correct. The guide describes supporting authority review as best practice.
The commission supplies no agency authority.

questions.stem: An Oregon affidavit was signed at home. Its jurat says signed and sworn before me. What must occur at the appointment?
options: A witness's promise about the contents
A present oath or affirmation and signing before the notary
Only recognition of yesterday's handwriting
Only the notary's stamp
questions.explanation: The guide requires personal participation, an oath or affirmation and present signing.
feedback: The affiant must make the truth declaration.
Correct. The guide requires personal participation, an oath or affirmation and present signing.
A jurat requires more than acknowledgment of handwriting.
A stamp does not administer an oath.

questions.stem: An Oregon affiant objects to invoking a deity. What equivalent procedure is available?
options: A solemn affirmation
No truthful-statement procedure is available
An employer signs the oath instead
An acknowledgment silently replaces the jurat
questions.explanation: The guide treats affirmation as legally equivalent to an oath.
feedback: Correct. The guide treats affirmation as legally equivalent to an oath.
Affirmation is an available alternative.
The affiant must personally participate.
The requested act cannot be silently changed.

questions.stem: A business agent offers to swear a personal truth oath on behalf of an absent principal. What principle applies?
options: Any agency document transfers personal oath-taking
A corporation can swear through an empty signature line
The notary may supply the truth statement
An oath cannot be made on someone else's behalf
questions.explanation: The oath-taker personally makes the truth commitment.
feedback: Agency does not transfer the personal oath.
An actual individual must take the oath.
The notary cannot make the affiant's oath.
Correct. The oath-taker personally makes the truth commitment.

questions.stem: During an Oregon jurat the signer remains silent after the notary asks the truthfulness question. What is missing?
options: A stamp-vendor witness
A separate acknowledgment of payment
The signer's assent to the oath or affirmation
A second seal impression
questions.explanation: The guide describes verbal assent or repetition as the oath-taker's response.
feedback: The vendor has no role in assent.
Payment acknowledgment does not complete the oath.
Correct. The guide describes verbal assent or repetition as the oath-taker's response.
Another impression does not provide assent.

questions.stem: An Oregon signature-witnessing certificate accompanies a previously signed record. What should the signer do?
options: Send a photograph of the signing
Sign again in the notary's presence
Only confirm the old signature
Ask the notary to trace the signature
questions.explanation: The guide requires actual witnessing for this act.
feedback: A photograph does not establish present witnessing.
Correct. The guide requires actual witnessing for this act.
That is insufficient for signature witnessing.
The notary cannot fabricate the signer's signature.

questions.stem: Two Oregon signers appear on different days for signature witnessing. How should certificates be handled?
options: Use a separate certificate for each act
List both as appearing together
Leave the certificate date blank
Use the second date for both
questions.explanation: Different appearance times require separate certificates under the guide.
feedback: Correct. Different appearance times require separate certificates under the guide.
That would misstate appearances.
The act date must be recorded.
That would misdate the earlier act.

questions.stem: A customer gives an Oregon notary a copy whose right margin is cropped. What must a copy certification establish?
options: Only that the central text looks similar
Only that the owner approves it
Only that the paper is new
A full, true and accurate reproduction including the margins
questions.explanation: The guide specifically requires a complete reproduction.
feedback: Missing margins can omit information.
Approval does not establish copy accuracy.
Paper age does not establish completeness.
Correct. The guide specifically requires a complete reproduction.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary is asked to certify a copy of a copy and the certificate does not claim an original was used. Is that necessarily barred?
options: No, so falsely label it an original
Only if the notary guarantees authorship
No, accurately describe the item actually copied
Yes, every copy must come from an original
questions.explanation: The guide permits copy-of-copy certification with truthful certificate wording.
feedback: The certificate must accurately describe the source.
Copy certification does not guarantee authorship.
Correct. The guide permits copy-of-copy certification with truthful certificate wording.
The guide expressly allows the qualified situation.

questions.stem: An Oregon customer wants the notary to certify a copy made in another office without comparison. What should the notary do?
options: Add an acknowledgment instead without asking
Make or carefully oversee and compare the reproduction
Rely solely on the customer's promise
Certify only the paper's color
questions.explanation: The notary bears responsibility for the copy's completeness and accuracy.
feedback: The act cannot be substituted unilaterally.
Correct. The notary bears responsibility for the copy's completeness and accuracy.
That does not complete the notary's determination.
The required determination concerns the record.

questions.stem: A customer asks an Oregon notary for a certified copy of filed articles of incorporation. Which source does the guide identify?
options: The Corporation Division holding the record
The notary's personal printer
A retail stamp maker
Any neighbor who has read the articles
questions.explanation: Certified copies of those public records should come from their custodian.
feedback: Correct. Certified copies of those public records should come from their custodian.
Printing does not create a custodian-certified copy.
A supplier does not hold the public record.
Reading does not confer custodial authority.

questions.stem: An Oregon customer seeks a faithful copy of a private letter. Which aspect of certification does the notary address?
options: Whether every claim in the letter is legally true
Whether the writer deserves credit
Whether the letter creates an enforceable contract
Whether the reproduction accurately matches the source
questions.explanation: Copy certification concerns the copy's fidelity.
feedback: Copy certification does not adjudicate the contents.
Creditworthiness is outside this act.
Enforceability is a legal determination.
Correct. Copy certification concerns the copy's fidelity.

questions.stem: An Oregon customer brings only a portrait and asks the notary to notarize the picture itself. What option does the guide describe?
options: Certify the portrait artist's reputation
Sign an otherwise blank photo reverse
Notarize an appropriate signed statement about the photograph
Stamp the face as proof of identity
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes the photograph from a person's notarizable statement.
feedback: Reputation is not the requested notarial act.
A bare signature and stamp lack a certificate.
Correct. The guide distinguishes the photograph from a person's notarizable statement.
Stamping a face does not create a notarial act.

questions.stem: A proposed Oregon copy-certification document bears a Do Not Copy warning. What should the notary check?
options: Whether the customer likes the warning
The issuing agency's copying restrictions
Whether the paper fits the copier
Whether the fee has been prepaid
questions.explanation: The guide directs attention to copying warnings and agency guidance.
feedback: Preference does not determine legal authority.
Correct. The guide directs attention to copying warnings and agency guidance.
Physical fit does not resolve restrictions.
Payment does not override restrictions.

questions.stem: An Oregon signer with a broken hand directs a friend to sign the signer's name before the notary. What special certificate fact is needed?
options: Identify who signed at whose direction
State the notary signed the principal's name
State the friend owns the document
Pretend the principal handwrote the signature
questions.explanation: The guide provides directed-signature wording identifying both people.
feedback: Correct. The guide provides directed-signature wording identifying both people.
The notary is not the directed third-party signer.
Direction does not transfer ownership.
The certificate must describe the actual procedure.

questions.stem: A companion signs an Oregon principal's name without the principal giving direction. What essential element of the guide's third-party procedure is absent?
options: A matching pen color
An employer's fee approval
A longer certificate title
The principal's direction to the other signer
questions.explanation: The special procedure depends on the principal directing the signature.
feedback: Pen color does not supply direction.
Fee approval does not authorize another person's signature.
A title does not establish the missing direction.
Correct. The special procedure depends on the principal directing the signature.

questions.stem: An ordinary Oregon notary receives a commercial-protest request and has no qualifying financial-institution or Oregon Bar connection. What should the notary do?
options: Use a copy-certification form
Charge extra to acquire qualification
Refer the specialized act to a qualified officer
Accept because every commissioned notary is qualified
questions.explanation: The guide restricts commercial protests to specified qualified notaries.
feedback: A different form does not create protest authority.
A fee does not supply the required connection.
Correct. The guide restricts commercial protests to specified qualified notaries.
The act has additional qualification limits.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary performs only jurats but has no journal available for an unexpected acknowledgment. What does the guide require?
options: Use the customer's diary
Maintain a journal even when usual acts are exempt
No journal until the first complaint
Borrow a shared office journal
questions.explanation: The guide requires keeping a journal available despite the usual act category.
feedback: The notary needs a compliant personal journal.
Correct. The guide requires keeping a journal available despite the usual act category.
Readiness is required before a nonexempt act.
Notaries cannot share an office journal.

questions.stem: A customer offers to return next week to sign the Oregon acknowledgment's journal entry. May the notary complete the act now?
options: No, complete the required entry contemporaneously
Yes, if the signature is familiar
Yes, if the notary remembers the customer
Only when the document has one page
questions.explanation: The guide prohibits finishing the entry after the signer leaves.
feedback: Correct. The guide prohibits finishing the entry after the signer leaves.
Familiarity does not defer the record.
Memory does not replace the required signature.
Page count does not control timing.

questions.stem: Before an Oregon appointment, a notary fills an entry saying the customer appeared and signed. Why is that premature?
options: Advance entries guarantee attendance
A calendar entry becomes sworn evidence
Payment confirms the signing
The journal must record the act that actually occurs
questions.explanation: The guide prohibits pre-filling the notarial event.
feedback: A reservation does not prove appearance.
A calendar does not establish the completed act.
Payment does not establish participation.
Correct. The guide prohibits pre-filling the notarial event.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary proposes an editable spreadsheet without tamper controls as the journal. What problem does the guide identify?
options: The spreadsheet must list property values
Only the font must change
It is not a proper journal format
Electronic journals are always forbidden
questions.explanation: The guide expressly rejects an ordinary Excel spreadsheet as the journal.
feedback: Property values do not cure format defects.
Typography does not establish tamper protection.
Correct. The guide expressly rejects an ordinary Excel spreadsheet as the journal.
Compliant electronic journals are allowed.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary wants removable journal pages in a three-ring binder. Which requirement is undermined?
options: The applicant's education number
Integrity and sequence of the journal records
The customer's choice of ink
The notary's travel policy
questions.explanation: The guide rejects loose-leaf binders as a journal format.
feedback: An education number does not secure entries.
Correct. The guide rejects loose-leaf binders as a journal format.
Customer ink does not cure removable pages.
Travel billing does not govern journal format.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary keeps work acts electronically and personal acts in a compliant paper journal. Is using both formats barred?
options: No, multiple compliant journals and formats are permitted
Yes, every notary must use exactly one book
Yes, electronic journals are only for lawyers
No, so coworkers may share both
questions.explanation: The guide permits more than one journal in either or both formats.
feedback: Correct. The guide permits more than one journal in either or both formats.
Oregon permits multiple journals.
The guide creates no lawyer-only rule.
Multiple personal journals do not authorize sharing.

questions.stem: An Oregon IPEN notary occasionally records electronic acts in a compliant paper journal. What does the guide say about that medium choice?
options: Every electronic act requires a new paper book
Paper journals authorize RON by themselves
Journal format removes identification duties
A paper journal may record electronic notarizations
questions.explanation: The guide permits paper records for electronic acts outside the separate RON requirement.
feedback: The guide does not impose that restriction.
RON has separate electronic-journal requirements.
Identity checks remain necessary.
Correct. The guide permits paper records for electronic acts outside the separate RON requirement.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary retires with the latest journal entry made this year. What starts the minimum retention clock?
options: The beginning of the first commission
The retirement party date
The last act recorded in that journal
The date the journal was bought
questions.explanation: The guide requires at least ten years after the last recorded act.
feedback: The last recorded act controls.
Retirement itself is not the statutory measuring event.
Correct. The guide requires at least ten years after the last recorded act.
Purchase does not start this retention period.

questions.stem: The required Oregon retention period has ended and the notary chooses lawful disposal. Which method does the guide describe?
options: Leave it in a public waiting room
Destroy it so personal information cannot be retrieved
Put intact pages in ordinary recycling
Sell it as a used notebook
questions.explanation: The guide gives secure destruction examples such as shredding.
feedback: That is not secure disposal.
Correct. The guide gives secure destruction examples such as shredding.
Personal information remains recoverable.
That exposes protected signer information.

questions.stem: An Oregon employer retained a journal under a valid agreement. Do the retention and disclosure rules disappear?
options: No, the employer must follow the same rules
Yes, business records have no restrictions
Only the fee entries need retention
A manager may publish every signature
questions.explanation: The guide expressly preserves the rules after agreed employer retention.
feedback: Correct. The guide expressly preserves the rules after agreed employer retention.
The guide preserves these duties.
Retention covers the journal.
The agreement does not waive disclosure protections.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary's commission is revoked. What document-handling deadline does the guide identify?
options: Keep notarizing until surrender
Destroy the journal immediately
Send only an employer reference
File the journal and stamp with the state within thirty days
questions.explanation: The guide gives a thirty-day revocation surrender period.
feedback: Revocation ends authority.
The guide requires filing it with the state.
A reference does not satisfy surrender.
Correct. The guide gives a thirty-day revocation surrender period.

questions.stem: An active Oregon notary dies without an employer journal agreement. What does the guide direct concerning the journal?
options: Sell the signed pages
Dispose of it with household recycling
Send it to the Secretary of State
Give it to another notary to continue entries
questions.explanation: The guide specifies state delivery upon the active notary's death.
feedback: Signer information is not merchandise.
The guide requires a custody process.
Correct. The guide specifies state delivery upon the active notary's death.
Another notary cannot continue the deceased notary's journal.

questions.stem: After an Oregon notary dies, a relative keeps the stamp as an operable office tool. What should happen?
options: Loan it to a coworker
Render it unusable through an allowed method
Transfer the commission to the relative
Keep using it for urgent family matters
questions.explanation: The guide directs disabling the deceased notary's stamping device.
feedback: A coworker cannot use that device for acts.
Correct. The guide directs disabling the deceased notary's stamping device.
A commission is not inherited.
The deceased notary's authority cannot be used.

questions.stem: An Oregon commission is temporarily suspended. How does the guide distinguish custody from authority?
options: Retain the journal and device while performing no suspended acts
Surrender the stamp to any customer
Continue acts because the tools remain in hand
Erase all evidence of the suspended period
questions.explanation: The guide says suspended notaries retain the tools until suspension ends.
feedback: Correct. The guide says suspended notaries retain the tools until suspension ends.
That is not the stated custody instruction.
Possession does not overcome suspension.
Journal integrity must be preserved.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary resigns and still has a working official stamp. What step accompanies resignation?
options: Donate it to a new applicant
Keep stamping until the printed expiration
Only change the ink color
Disable the stamping device
questions.explanation: The guide requires the device to be rendered unusable on resignation.
feedback: The device identifies the resigning notary.
Resignation ends the authority earlier.
Color changes do not disable the stamp.
Correct. The guide requires the device to be rendered unusable on resignation.

questions.stem: An Oregon private-sector notary receives a subpoena for a journal entry. Can ordinary journal privacy be used to ignore it?
options: Yes, if the customer paid cash
Only respond by destroying the entry
No, subpoenas are a stated disclosure exception
Yes, a journal is always absolutely secret
questions.explanation: The guide identifies subpoenas and state requests as required-disclosure routes.
feedback: Payment method does not remove the subpoena.
Destruction does not satisfy lawful disclosure.
Correct. The guide identifies subpoenas and state requests as required-disclosure routes.
The guide states exceptions.

questions.stem: An Oregon public employee's notarial journal receives a public-records request. Which distinction matters?
options: Only the notary's age controls disclosure
Public-record disclosure laws may apply to that journal
All notarial journals are outside public-record laws
The employer may automatically publish the full book
questions.explanation: The guide distinguishes public officials' or employees' journals from ordinary private-sector journals.
feedback: Age does not determine this distinction.
Correct. The guide distinguishes public officials' or employees' journals from ordinary private-sector journals.
The guide identifies public-sector treatment.
The relevant public-record process and restrictions still matter.

questions.stem: An Oregon signer is permitted to inspect their own journal entry. What should the notary do with neighboring entries?
options: Cover unrelated entries to protect other signers
Expose the full page for convenience
Read every signature aloud
Ask the signer to erase the others
questions.explanation: The guide directs privacy protection for entries above and below.
feedback: Correct. The guide directs privacy protection for entries above and below.
Other signers' information should be concealed.
That needlessly discloses unrelated data.
Entries must not be destroyed.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary starts using shorthand such as ACK and CW in journal entries. What addition does the guide recommend?
options: A different meaning on every page
A secret code never explained
Replacing all signer names with shorthand
A glossary explaining abbreviations and symbols
questions.explanation: The guide recommends an explanatory glossary in the journal front.
feedback: Inconsistent notation undermines clarity.
The record should remain understandable.
Required identity information must remain recorded.
Correct. The guide recommends an explanatory glossary in the journal front.

questions.stem: A journal entry for an Oregon acknowledgment lists a document date but omits when the act occurred. Which information is missing?
options: The recipient's lunch schedule
The notary's exam score
The date and time of the notarial act
The paper's retail price
questions.explanation: The guide lists act timing separately from document date.
feedback: That is irrelevant to act timing.
That is not required act timing.
Correct. The guide lists act timing separately from document date.
That is not the missing act information.

questions.stem: An Oregon journal records only Government ID without issuer, type or expiration. What should the identification description provide?
options: The notary's guess at nationality
Issuer, document type and expiration date
The entire Social Security number
Only the card's color
questions.explanation: The guide specifies these credential-description elements.
feedback: Nationality guesses do not describe the credential.
Correct. The guide specifies these credential-description elements.
That personal number should not be recorded.
Color does not supply the listed detail.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary wants to record a full passport number for added security. What does the guide direct?
options: Do not record that personal number
Record it because more data is always better
Publish it with the journal entry
Copy it into the stamp impression
questions.explanation: The guide excludes passport, driver's-license and Social Security numbers.
feedback: Correct. The guide excludes passport, driver's-license and Social Security numbers.
The guide specifically warns against these numbers.
Public exposure compounds the issue.
The stamp does not carry customer identity numbers.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary waives an acknowledgment fee. What should the fee field show?
options: Leave it deliberately ambiguous
The maximum as if collected
The customer's bank balance
A no-charge notation
questions.explanation: The guide calls for a notation when no fee is collected.
feedback: The record should show the fee was waived.
That would misstate the charge.
That is irrelevant sensitive information.
Correct. The guide calls for a notation when no fee is collected.

questions.stem: Five duplicate originals are notarized for one Oregon signer on the same day. Which shortcut does the guide permit?
options: One entry omitting the number
Reuse last month's signature without a new record
One entry stating the number of duplicate originals
No entry because the texts match
questions.explanation: The guide permits that specifically described duplicate-original shortcut.
feedback: The shortcut should indicate how many originals.
The shortcut concerns the same date and signer.
Correct. The guide permits that specifically described duplicate-original shortcut.
The acts still require documentation.

questions.stem: An Oregon signer presents different documents on the same day. How may a combined entry describe them?
options: Let the signer choose a false common date
List the distinct acts, document dates and document types
Record only the first document
Call all documents one unspecified paper
questions.explanation: The guide permits combining while preserving the distinct information.
feedback: Dates must remain accurate.
Correct. The guide permits combining while preserving the distinct information.
That omits the other acts.
The distinct documents and acts need identification.

questions.stem: Using Oregon's separate-line shortcut for one signer and several same-day acts, what may avoid repeating identical details?
options: Ditto marks for information that is actually the same
Ditto marks for facts that differ
Removing the signer's identity entirely
Using another customer's address
questions.explanation: The guide permits the described repeated-information shortcut.
feedback: Correct. The guide permits the described repeated-information shortcut.
The shortcut cannot make different facts identical.
Required identity information must remain ascertainable.
That misidentifies the signer.

questions.stem: An Oregon repeat signer returns on a later date. Which previous-entry reference does the guide permit?
options: Reuse the earlier act date
Pretend no new appearance occurred
Automatically carry over every earlier signature
Refer to the earlier address and identification description
questions.explanation: The guide permits previous-entry citation for those specified details.
feedback: The new act has its own date.
A new act still needs its record.
The permitted reference is narrower.
Correct. The guide permits previous-entry citation for those specified details.

questions.stem: Two Oregon notaries work alternate shifts and want one office journal. What should their recordkeeping arrangement be?
options: Let the manager sign all entries
One book owned by the stamp vendor
A separate journal for each notary
One journal with no notary names
questions.explanation: The guide expressly prohibits shared office journals.
feedback: The manager cannot replace each notary's acts.
Vendor ownership does not satisfy the individual duty.
Correct. The guide expressly prohibits shared office journals.
That removes accountability.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary receives a new stamp with one digit missing from the commission number. What should happen before use?
options: Write the missing digit only on the receipt
Correct the stamp to match the issued commission
Use it until a complaint is filed
Borrow a coworker's stamp
questions.explanation: The guide directs checking complete and correct stamp information.
feedback: The stamp itself remains defective.
Correct. The guide directs checking complete and correct stamp information.
Known incorrect commission information should be corrected first.
A coworker's stamp identifies a different official.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary owns an embossed seal and an official ink stamp. Which tool performs the official stamping function?
options: The compliant official stamp
The embosser alone in every case
A company logo stamp
Any stamp selected by the customer
questions.explanation: The guide permits an embosser only as an unofficial protection device.
feedback: Correct. The guide permits an embosser only as an unofficial protection device.
It does not replace the official stamp.
The logo lacks the required commission identity.
Customer preference cannot replace required equipment.

questions.stem: A form preprints Washington as the venue but the Oregon act occurs in Marion County. What should the certificate show?
options: Washington because it was preprinted
The county where the document will be filed
The signer's birthplace
Oregon and the actual county of the act
questions.explanation: Venue identifies where the notarial act occurs.
feedback: Preprinting does not override the actual location.
Filing location is not act venue.
Birthplace does not identify this act's venue.
Correct. Venue identifies where the notarial act occurs.

questions.stem: An Oregon certificate has the date, signer name and stamp but lacks the notary's signature. Is the certificate complete?
options: Yes, a receipt supplies the signature
Only if the signer signs for the notary
No, the notary must sign
Yes, the stamp substitutes for signing
questions.explanation: The guide lists the notary signature as an essential component.
feedback: A receipt does not execute the certificate.
The signer cannot supply the official signature.
Correct. The guide lists the notary signature as an essential component.
The signature is separately required.

questions.stem: An Oregon certificate places the signature on the front and its stamp alone on the reverse. What arrangement does the guide require?
options: The signer may move the stamp later
All certificate components on the same page and side
Any separate pages if the paper color matches
A stamp only on the envelope
questions.explanation: The guide requires the components together on one side.
feedback: The notary must complete the certificate properly.
Correct. The guide requires the components together on one side.
Color does not join the certificate components.
The envelope is not the certificate.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary handles a qualifying subdivision plat on Mylar that will not hold the ordinary stamp ink. What exception does the guide describe?
options: Use the prescribed printed commission information beneath the signature
Omit all commission information
Use the developer's corporate seal
Treat every plastic document as a plat
questions.explanation: The plat exception substitutes specified notary identification details.
feedback: Correct. The plat exception substitutes specified notary identification details.
The exception still requires prescribed information.
That does not identify the notary.
The exception concerns specified plat categories.

questions.stem: A qualifying Oregon plat uses the no-imprint exception but omits the commission number. What is missing?
options: The customer's exam score
A second witness's address
A travel-fee agreement printed on the plat
The prescribed commission-number statement
questions.explanation: The guide requires commission number among the substituted identification details.
feedback: That is not prescribed plat information.
That does not replace commission identification.
Fees do not cure missing official details.
Correct. The guide requires commission number among the substituted identification details.

questions.stem: A customer insists on certificate wording that the Oregon notary knows is false. Does insistence permit signing it?
options: Yes, if the notary notes the demand
Only if the fee is waived
No, known false statements cannot be certified
Yes, customer insistence transfers responsibility
questions.explanation: The guide prohibits executing a knowingly false certificate.
feedback: A journal note does not authorize a false certificate.
A free act must still be truthful.
Correct. The guide prohibits executing a knowingly false certificate.
The notary retains responsibility for the certificate.

questions.stem: An Oregon certificate reads before me [blank], personally appeared [blank]. Where should the notary's name go?
options: In neither blank if a stamp is present
In the first blank identifying the official
In both blanks regardless of the signer
Only in the signer's blank
questions.explanation: The guide warns against putting the official's name in the signer's blank.
feedback: The particulars still need completion.
Correct. The guide warns against putting the official's name in the signer's blank.
That misidentifies the appearing person.
The signer and official have different roles.

questions.stem: An Oregon form says subscribed and sworn. Which paired procedure does that wording signal?
options: Witness the signature and administer an oath or affirmation
Only observe the paper being printed
Only confirm the signer paid
Certify the document is legally enforceable
questions.explanation: The guide expressly links that wording to both procedures.
feedback: Correct. The guide expressly links that wording to both procedures.
Printing is not the jurat ceremony.
Payment is not sworn execution.
That exceeds the notarial act.

questions.stem: An Oregon certificate has no space for all required particulars. What should the notary do after the customer selects the appropriate act?
options: Crowd incomplete fragments around the stamp
Sign a blank sheet for later use
Let the recipient add the notary's signature
Complete and securely attach a proper certificate
questions.explanation: The guide permits an attached certificate when needed.
feedback: Required information must remain clear and complete.
A blank certificate creates misuse risk.
Only the notary executes that signature.
Correct. The guide permits an attached certificate when needed.

questions.stem: The Oregon customer has already left when an office assistant notices a certificate error. Who should make the correction?
options: The document recipient without contacting the notary
A stamp seller on request
The notary who completed the certificate
Any assistant who knows the file
questions.explanation: The guide prohibits allowing someone else to change the certificate.
feedback: The recipient cannot alter the official certificate.
A supplier does not control the completed act.
Correct. The guide prohibits allowing someone else to change the certificate.
File knowledge does not transfer correction responsibility.

questions.stem: An Oregon notary repairs a certificate while the signer remains present. What correction method does the guide recommend?
options: Leave an unsigned replacement page
Line through the error, add the correction and initial and date it
Erase the original with white-out
Have the signer overwrite the notary's words
questions.explanation: The guide preserves the original text and identifies the correction.
feedback: The certificate must be properly executed.
Correct. The guide preserves the original text and identifies the correction.
