Only the age of the uploaded filename
Only the platform's subscription price
questions.explanation: The rule requires the signer to possess the credential then.
feedback: An uploaded image alone does not establish present possession.
Correct. The rule requires the signer to possess the credential then.
Filename age is not possession.
Price does not establish possession.

questions.stem: An Oregon RON ID upload is so blurred that its text and security features cannot be inspected. What should be obtained?
options: Images of sufficient quality for analysis and visual inspection
A larger fee for using a blurred image
A verbal description without credential analysis
A cropped social-media avatar
questions.explanation: The rule requires legible, sufficiently clear credential images.
feedback: Correct. The rule requires legible, sufficiently clear credential images.
Fees do not repair the missing visual evidence.
The prescribed analysis still must occur.
That does not show the credential features.

questions.stem: A vendor's Oregon identity quiz uses five questions with only two choices each. What must be corrected?
options: Reduce the quiz to one question
Replace the quiz with the notary's exam score
Use the signer's home-made questions only
Provide at least five answer choices per question
questions.explanation: The identity-proofing rule sets a minimum of five choices.
feedback: The rule requires five questions.
The customer's identity quiz has a different purpose.
The rule calls for questions from data sources.
Correct. The identity-proofing rule sets a minimum of five choices.

questions.stem: An Oregon remote signer answers three of the five identity questions correctly within two minutes. Does that meet the KBA threshold?
options: Yes, speed eliminates wrong answers
Only if the notary also signs the quiz
No, eighty percent requires four correct answers
Yes, a simple majority is sufficient
questions.explanation: The rule requires eighty percent correct within two minutes.
feedback: The score requirement still applies.
The notary cannot cure the customer's result by signing.
Correct. The rule requires eighty percent correct within two minutes.
Three of five falls short of eighty percent.

questions.stem: After an Oregon signer's first failed KBA quiz, the platform offers unlimited immediate attempts over a week. What limit does the rule provide?
options: One retake only after a full year
Up to two additional quizzes within forty-eight hours
Unlimited quizzes for every paid customer
No retake under any circumstances
questions.explanation: The rule limits the additional attempts after first failure.
feedback: That is not the prescribed limit.
Correct. The rule limits the additional attempts after first failure.
Payment does not remove the stated limit.
The rule permits limited additional attempts.

questions.stem: An Oregon KBA retake repeats all five earlier questions. What change does the rule require?
options: Replace at least two prior questions
Replace only the background color
Keep all questions if the order changes
Replace the signer's name with initials
questions.explanation: The rule requires forty percent replacement on a retake.
feedback: Correct. The rule requires forty percent replacement on a retake.
Cosmetic changes do not replace questions.
Reordering does not satisfy replacement.
Name formatting does not change the questions.

questions.stem: An Oregon signer exits the notarial session and returns later expecting to resume after the identity step. What does the rule require?
options: Resume with no renewed identity workflow
Rely only on the earlier fee receipt
Delete the initial session record silently
Restart credential analysis and KBA from the beginning
questions.explanation: The rule requires restart after the signer exits the act.
feedback: The rule directs a restart.
A receipt does not restart identity proofing.
Deletion is not the required verification response.
Correct. The rule requires restart after the signer exits the act.

questions.stem: An Oregon RON document can be edited after completion with no evidence of change. Which required property is missing?
options: A paper staple
A larger file name
Tamper evidence
A decorative border
questions.explanation: The rule requires completed documents to be electronically signed and rendered tamper-evident.
feedback: A staple does not secure the electronic original.
Naming does not provide tamper evidence.
Correct. The rule requires completed documents to be electronically signed and rendered tamper-evident.
A border does not reveal later edits.

questions.stem: An Oregon vendor keeps RON transaction records for only one year. Which minimum does the rule require?
options: Only until the notary's vacation
Ten years following the notarization
One month after payment
Until the signer downloads a copy
questions.explanation: The technology rule gives a ten-year transaction-record period.
feedback: Personal scheduling does not define retention.
Correct. The technology rule gives a ten-year transaction-record period.
Payment does not set this period.
Download does not end retention.

questions.stem: A remote session's audio repeatedly drops so the Oregon notary cannot understand the signer. Which response fits the technology standard?
options: Stop until adequate reliable communication is available
Complete the oath through guesses
Ignore audio because video is visible
Have a silent bystander nod for the signer
questions.explanation: The rule calls for clear, continuous synchronous audio and video.
feedback: Correct. The rule calls for clear, continuous synchronous audio and video.
Guessing does not establish communication.
Both sight and sound are required.
A bystander cannot supply the signer's participation.

questions.stem: An Oregon RON archive stores a video file with no connection to the electronic journal entry. What organization is required?
options: Sort all recordings only by file size
Keep the link only in a customer's memory
Delete the journal after exporting video
Logically associate the recording with the electronic journal
questions.explanation: The rule requires that association.
feedback: File size does not link the particular act.
The archival association must be maintained.
The journal remains a separate required record.
Correct. The rule requires that association.

questions.stem: An Oregon vendor stores recordings in a format that nobody can play without a discontinued proprietary device. Which standard is implicated?
options: The notary's exam ranking
The customer's printer speed
Viewability and audibility through broadly available players
The price of the original laptop
questions.explanation: The rule requires recordings usable through broadly available audio/video players.
feedback: Exam scores do not resolve archival usability.
Printing does not play audiovisual records.
Correct. The rule requires recordings usable through broadly available audio/video players.
Price does not establish future playback.

questions.stem: A proposed Oregon RON recording embeds the entire transaction document into the video itself. What does the rule direct?
options: Delete all executed electronic records
Do not record the executed transaction documents as part of the video
Include every document page in the recording automatically
Replace the person-to-person interaction with document images
questions.explanation: The rule separates transaction documents from the audiovisual interaction recording.
feedback: The rule does not authorize deleting transaction records.
Correct. The rule separates transaction documents from the audiovisual interaction recording.
The rule prohibits this inclusion.
The interaction itself must be recorded.

cards.title: Authority calendar
cards.front: Which dates should be tracked separately?
cards.rule: Education recency, application timing and commission expiration serve different purposes.
cards.boundary: The new term still requires Basics.
cards.mixup: A reminder never extends authority.

cards.title: Names on the commission
cards.front: How should the commission identify the applicant?
cards.rule: Use the full legal first, middle and last names supported by identification.
cards.boundary: The verified customary signature may have a shorter form.
cards.mixup: Printed legal name and handwriting are different fields.

cards.title: Training evidence
cards.front: What does course completion accomplish?
cards.rule: It satisfies the approved education prerequisite for the state application process.
cards.boundary: It does not issue a commission.
cards.mixup: A training receipt cannot authorize acts.

cards.title: The oath stage
cards.front: Why use the emailed state form carefully?
cards.rule: The application section reflects the state's process and should not be altered.
cards.boundary: Return the notarized oath within the prescribed period.
cards.mixup: Recreating the form from memory can change official details.

cards.title: Manufacturing authorization
cards.front: What information does a stamp maker verify?
cards.rule: The authorization certificate supplies the commissioned name, number and expiration.
cards.boundary: A supply purchase does not appoint the applicant.
cards.mixup: The vendor cannot invent a commission number.

cards.title: Statewide work
cards.front: What geographic scope does an Oregon commission provide?
cards.rule: The notary may act throughout Oregon with the actual county in the venue.
cards.boundary: Physical presence outside Oregon is beyond that authority.
cards.mixup: The mailing address does not determine every venue.

cards.title: Prices before service
cards.front: When should the customer learn the price?
cards.rule: Display or provide the fee schedule before notarization.
cards.boundary: Additional charges belong in the advance disclosure.
cards.mixup: A journal fee field does not inform the customer beforehand.

cards.title: Waiver duration
cards.front: What does a filed fee waiver change?
cards.rule: It prevents charging until properly rescinded.
cards.boundary: It also follows the notary's personal after-hours acts.
cards.mixup: A one-time free act is different from a filed waiver.

cards.title: Travel quote
cards.front: How should mobile-service pricing be arranged?
cards.rule: Agree on travel charges before meeting and identify them separately.
cards.boundary: The act fee retains its own limit.
cards.mixup: Arrival cannot create advance agreement retroactively.

cards.title: Legal-practice boundary
cards.front: What work exceeds a nonattorney commission?
cards.rule: Choosing legal procedures or drafting legal records outside a qualifying capacity.
cards.boundary: Free favors can still involve legal practice.
cards.mixup: Familiarity with a form is not a law license.

cards.title: Accessible advertising
cards.front: Who should understand the required warning?
cards.rule: The ad's audience should receive the warning in the advertisement's language.
cards.boundary: Print, internet and broadcast media are covered.
cards.mixup: Changing media does not remove the warning.

cards.title: Workplace policies
cards.front: What may an employer regulate?
cards.rule: Workplace access may be limited through lawful nondiscriminatory policies.
cards.boundary: No policy authorizes false notarization.
cards.mixup: Employment does not transfer the commission.

cards.title: Liability and care
cards.front: What does insurance leave unchanged?
cards.rule: The notary must perform every legal safeguard despite insurance coverage.
cards.boundary: Policy limits do not cap all potential damages.
cards.mixup: Insurance cannot authorize deliberate misconduct.

cards.title: Customer choice
cards.front: How can the notary help a customer choose an act?
cards.rule: Explain authorized acts neutrally and refer legal uncertainty to an adviser.
cards.boundary: Do not choose a certificate for legal advantage.
cards.mixup: The most familiar certificate may not serve the customer's purpose.

cards.title: Venue truth
cards.front: What does the venue locate?
cards.rule: It identifies the state and county of the act.
cards.boundary: Correct inconsistent preprinting.
cards.mixup: Document destination does not determine venue.

cards.title: Acknowledgment dates
cards.front: How can two dates both be accurate?
cards.rule: A signature may predate its acknowledgment, while the certificate uses the act date.
cards.boundary: The signature cannot be made after the completed acknowledgment.
cards.mixup: An earlier signature does not justify backdating.

cards.title: Representative execution
cards.front: What does the representative acknowledge?
cards.rule: Execution with authority for the represented person or entity.
cards.boundary: Review of supporting authority is described as best practice.
cards.mixup: Identifying an officer does not guarantee company debts.

cards.title: Jurat meaning
cards.front: What procedure makes a jurat complete?
cards.rule: The identified participant appears, signs before the notary and swears or affirms truthfulness.
cards.boundary: A genuine earlier signature does not replace present signing.
cards.mixup: Acknowledgment alone omits the truth commitment.

cards.title: Affirmation
cards.front: Why offer an affirmation?
cards.rule: It provides an equivalent solemn truth commitment without invoking a deity.
cards.boundary: The participant still must assent.
cards.mixup: An affirmation is not casual conversation.

cards.title: Witnessed signing
cards.front: What does signature witnessing certify?
cards.rule: The identified signer freely signs before the notary.
cards.boundary: A previously signed record needs present re-signing for this act.
cards.mixup: The acknowledgment timing rule does not govern signature witnessing.

cards.title: Credible witness chain
cards.front: Which relationships support witness identification?
cards.rule: The witness personally knows the signer and is known or satisfactorily identified by the notary.
cards.boundary: The witness also gives sworn or affirmed testimony.
cards.mixup: Knowing the notary alone does not identify the principal.

cards.title: Credential quality
cards.front: Why examine more than the date?
cards.rule: The credential must fit a permitted category and satisfactorily identify the person.
cards.boundary: Request additional evidence for unresolved mismatch or damage.
cards.mixup: A timely card can still show the wrong person.

cards.title: Physical inability
cards.front: How can a directed signature be described honestly?
cards.rule: Name the person who physically signs and the principal giving direction.
cards.boundary: The principal must direct the signature.
cards.mixup: Holding the pen does not create authority.

cards.title: Copy fidelity
cards.front: What does copy certification determine?
cards.rule: The reproduction is full, true and accurate, including margins.
cards.boundary: Screen public and vital records for restrictions.
cards.mixup: It does not certify the source's substantive truth.

cards.title: Custodian route
cards.front: Who supplies certified public-record copies?
cards.rule: The responsible public agency supplies its official certified copies.
cards.boundary: A private photocopy does not become a custodian copy through a stamp.
cards.mixup: The notary's commission does not replace the issuer.

cards.title: Supported repair
cards.front: What supports correction of a completed certificate?
cards.rule: Verify the facts from the journal or signer and record the repair.
cards.boundary: The notary personally makes the correction on the returned record.
cards.mixup: A detached signed certificate should not be sent for someone else to attach.

cards.title: Journal readiness
cards.front: Why keep a journal even for mostly exempt acts?
cards.rule: Oregon requires maintaining a journal ready for required acknowledgment and witnessing entries.
cards.boundary: Other ordinary acts are strongly recommended for recording.
cards.mixup: Keeping the book and recording an act are separate rules.

cards.title: Contemporaneous entries
cards.front: When is the proper record created?
cards.rule: Complete it with the notarization while the participant can sign.
cards.boundary: Do not pre-fill event facts or postpone recording.
cards.mixup: A reservation does not prove appearance.

cards.title: Medium integrity
cards.front: What matters in choosing a journal format?
cards.rule: Preserve entry sequence and prevent improper alteration under the rules.
cards.boundary: Ordinary spreadsheets and loose-leaf binders are unsuitable examples.
cards.mixup: Electronic convenience alone does not establish compliance.

cards.title: Limited identification data
cards.front: Which credential description belongs in the entry?
cards.rule: Record issuer, document type and expiration as required.
cards.boundary: Exclude full passport, driver's-license and Social Security numbers.
cards.mixup: Collecting more sensitive numbers does not improve compliance.

cards.title: A free act's record
cards.front: How should a fee waiver appear in the entry?
cards.rule: Make a clear no-charge notation.
cards.boundary: Do not record an uncollected fee as collected.
cards.mixup: An unexplained blank can obscure what occurred.

cards.title: Duplicate originals
cards.front: When does a combined entry fit duplicates?
cards.rule: For the same person and date, identify how many duplicate originals were notarized.
cards.boundary: Different records still need distinct descriptions.
cards.mixup: Identical text does not eliminate recordkeeping.

cards.title: A later appointment
cards.front: What earlier information may be referenced?
cards.rule: A later entry may cite prior address and identification descriptions under the guide.
cards.boundary: The new event still needs its own record.
cards.mixup: A prior entry cannot move the new act to an earlier date.

cards.title: One notary's accountability
cards.front: Why avoid a shared office journal?
cards.rule: Each notary maintains the record of that notary's acts.
cards.boundary: Several personal journals may exist within one office.
cards.mixup: Alternating shifts do not combine commissions.

cards.title: Employer agreement
cards.front: How may an employer retain a workplace journal?
cards.rule: Use the signed journal agreement and preserve a copy with the notary.
cards.boundary: The employer follows retention and disclosure rules.
cards.mixup: Paying for supplies alone does not create the agreement.

cards.title: Retention clock
cards.front: What event measures ten-year retention?
cards.rule: The last act recorded in the journal starts the minimum period.
cards.boundary: Resignation and renewal do not shorten it.
cards.mixup: The book's purchase date is not the measuring event.

cards.title: Privacy during access
cards.front: How can the record be inspected selectively?
cards.rule: Cover unrelated entries and follow the applicable access procedure.
cards.boundary: Public-employee journals may have public-record treatment.
cards.mixup: A private journal is not an unrestricted address directory.

cards.title: A term ends
cards.front: What happens to records and equipment?
cards.rule: Disable the expired stamp while preserving required journal retention.
cards.boundary: A new term can reuse the journal after updating its front information.
cards.mixup: A pending application does not extend the old stamp's authority.

cards.title: Recovered stamp
cards.front: What follows recovery after replacement?
cards.rule: Report recovery as directed and destroy the original stamp.
cards.boundary: The guide requires a timely written explanation.
cards.mixup: Keeping both as interchangeable tools conflicts with that instruction.

cards.title: Glossary of entries
cards.front: Why explain journal abbreviations?
cards.rule: A glossary preserves the meaning of shorthand for future review.
cards.boundary: Use abbreviations consistently.
cards.mixup: A private unexplained code reduces the record's usefulness.

cards.title: Media and appearance
cards.front: What separates IPEN from RON?
cards.rule: IPEN combines electronic records with physical appearance. RON uses remote participation.
cards.boundary: The authorization processes are separate.
cards.mixup: A tablet alone does not make the signer remote.
cards.source: Remote and Electronic Notarization FAQs, RON and IPEN definitions

cards.title: State decision
cards.front: What completes the RON request process?
cards.rule: The state reviews the notice and sends an approving or rejecting acknowledgment.
cards.boundary: Begin remote acts after approval.
cards.mixup: Sending an email alone does not establish authority.
cards.source: Remote Online Notarization, Submit the RON Notice Form

cards.title: The next commission
cards.front: Why file another RON notice after renewal?
cards.rule: RON approval follows the specific commission and needs updating for the next term.
cards.boundary: The new term has its own number.
cards.mixup: A vendor subscription does not extend expired authority.
cards.source: Remote Online Notarization, Things to Remember

cards.title: Human review
cards.front: What remains after automated proofing?
cards.rule: Compare the live person's features and the credential visually.
cards.boundary: Do not complete when identity cannot be validated or matched.
cards.mixup: A platform success message does not replace comparison.

cards.title: Identity quiz
cards.front: What purpose does KBA serve?
cards.rule: Data-source questions help authenticate the remote participant.
cards.boundary: The five-question identity process is distinct from licensing testing.
cards.mixup: KBA specifications do not describe the commission examination.

cards.title: Restart after exit
cards.front: What follows the signer's exit from the act?
cards.rule: Restart credential analysis and KBA from the beginning.
cards.boundary: Earlier clearance does not survive the specified exit event.
cards.mixup: Returning to the call does not automatically restore the workflow.

cards.title: Recorded interaction
cards.front: What should the recording preserve?
cards.rule: Preserve the person-to-person interaction and associate it with the electronic journal.
cards.boundary: Transaction documents are excluded from the video itself.
cards.mixup: Document storage and recorded ceremony have different requirements.

cards.title: Usable archives
cards.front: What makes retention practically compliant?
cards.rule: Keep records safe, available to the state and playable through broadly available tools.
cards.boundary: Cancellation does not eliminate required retention.
cards.mixup: An unusable retained file fails the playback standard.

cards.title: Price the method
cards.front: Why classify the method before quoting?
cards.rule: The FAQ sets a twenty-five-dollar RON maximum and ten-dollar IPEN maximum.
cards.boundary: Apply advance travel agreement requirements where applicable.
cards.mixup: Electronic media do not automatically trigger the RON rate.
cards.source: Remote and Electronic Notarization FAQs, RON and IPEN fees

cards.title: Complete technology
cards.front: What must accompany the video connection?
cards.rule: Use tamper-evident documents, privacy, secure records and clear synchronous communication.
cards.boundary: Standalone video apps do not meet the complete RON process.
cards.mixup: A paid conferencing plan does not establish authorization.

commission.summary: Maintain the Oregon connection supporting appointment, finish each commissioning step and distinguish statutory authority from workplace arrangements. The official examination remains open book, with its unpublished numerical specifications left unknown.

sections.heading: Keep authority current
sections.body: The qualification and application materials require approved Basics, the state examination, background screening and completion of the oath process. The guide describes a four-year commission and a new application in the thirty days before expiration. An active notary also takes Basics for the next term under the requirement effective January 1, 2025. The emailed oath must be notarized and returned with the processing fee under the state instructions. Receiving training evidence or ordering supplies does not finish commissioning. Use the full legal commissioned name and an appropriately verified signature. Sources include the current qualification and application pages and Guide pp. 14–18.

sections.heading: Practice within the role
sections.body: Oregon commissions operate throughout the state, while the venue identifies the actual act location. An employer can regulate workplace access through lawful policies but cannot authorize false certificates or absent-signer shortcuts. Nonattorney notaries cannot choose legal procedures for customers. Advertising must carry the required warning in the advertisement language. Ordinary act fees are capped at ten dollars under the guide, subject to the separate RON fee category. Disclose fees beforehand and agree on travel before meeting. A filed waiver continues until properly rescinded. Guide pp. 20–29 supports these workplace, professional-scope and fee distinctions.

example.heading: An employment change during the term
example.body: A Portland bank employee leaves for another Oregon workplace while the commission remains active. The commission belongs to the individual. The notary updates contact details, keeps the stamp secure and checks whether a signed agreement governs the old workplace journal. The new employer can establish a lawful service schedule, but cannot excuse identification or certificate requirements. A previously filed fee waiver still governs after-hours acts until it is rescinded through the state process.

keyFacts: Basics and the examination recur for another Oregon commission.
An application or supply purchase does not activate authority.
A filed fee waiver applies beyond the workplace until rescinded.
Ordinary fees and travel charges require proper advance disclosure.

certificates.summary: Identify the requested act, confirm personal participation and identity, then complete a truthful certificate. The act determines signing and oath procedures.

sections.heading: Choose the procedure through the customer
sections.body: An acknowledgment can address a signature already made, but the person must appear and acknowledge voluntary execution. A jurat requires a present oath or affirmation and signing before the notary. Signature witnessing also requires present signing. Representative acknowledgment records execution for the represented person with the proper authority. A nonattorney notary can explain these acts neutrally but cannot choose the legally advantageous certificate. A credible witness must know the signer, be identified by the notary and provide the required sworn or affirmed testimony. See Guide pp. 31–33 and 40–55.

sections.heading: Complete and repair the evidence
sections.body: The certificate identifies the actual venue, date, participant and procedure and includes the required official signature and stamp information. Its components belong together on the same page and side, subject to the specific plat exception. A loose certificate must be completed and attached to the actual record. Copy certification requires a full, true and accurate reproduction and screening for public or vital records that belong with their official custodian. If a certificate needs repair, the original record returns, the notary verifies the facts and personally corrects it, and the journal records the change. See Guide pp. 40–44 and 56–60.

example.heading: A pre-signed insurance statement
example.body: A Bend customer brings a statement signed yesterday with a certificate saying signed and sworn before me. The request is a jurat. The notary identifies the participant, resolves willingness and capacity, administers the oath or affirmation and has the participant sign before the notary. The certificate uses the current act date. Merely acknowledging yesterday's signature would omit the jurat procedure.

keyFacts: Earlier signing is compatible with acknowledgment but does not replace present signing for a jurat or signature witnessing.
The appearing person must be satisfactorily identified.
A known false certificate cannot be completed at a customer's insistence.
Corrections require supported facts and the notary's own action.

records.summary: Preserve a reliable journal, protect private information and control the official stamp throughout changes in employment and commission status.

sections.heading: Create the record at the act
sections.body: The guide requires maintaining a journal and specifically requires ordinary acknowledgment and signature-witnessing entries. Other ordinary acts are strongly recommended for recording. Complete a required entry contemporaneously, with the signer present to sign. Record the act timing, type, document information, signer details, identification description and fee or no-charge notation. The guide directs recording issuer, credential type and expiration while excluding full passport, driver's-license and Social Security numbers. It permits defined shortcuts for duplicate originals, same-day multiple acts and references to prior address and identification details. Those shortcuts preserve the essential distinctions between acts. See Guide pp. 34–39.

sections.heading: Plan custody and final retention
sections.body: Every notary maintains separate records. Compliant paper and electronic formats can be used for ordinary acts, while ordinary editable spreadsheets and loose-leaf binders are unsuitable. Keep the journal for at least ten years after its last recorded act. A signed employer journal agreement can govern retention at departure, but the employer then follows the same retention and disclosure rules. The official stamp remains with the notary and is disabled at expiration or resignation as directed. Private-sector and public-employee journals have different disclosure contexts. Subpoenas and Secretary of State requests are recognized disclosure routes. See Guide pp. 18–21 and 35–37.

example.heading: A journal with two commission terms
example.body: An Eugene notary receives a new commission while the existing journal still has unused pages. The notary updates the required front information and marks where the new commission begins. Prior entries remain intact and retained. The expired stamp is disabled, and the new authorized stamp is used for the new term. The journal's ultimate retention clock runs from the last act later recorded in it.

keyFacts: Do not share a journal with another notary.
Required entries are contemporaneous with the act.
A journal agreement does not transfer the stamp.
The last recorded act starts the minimum ten-year retention period.

remote.summary: Distinguish RON from physical-appearance electronic work and satisfy the additional authorization, identity, recording and archival requirements.

sections.heading: Authorize the intended method
sections.body: The current state RON page requires a qualifying vendor, state RON training, vendor training and the notice submission with vendor-generated electronic signature and stamp samples. Wait for approval before performing remote acts. The notary is physically in Oregon, while the signer may participate remotely subject to the applicable conditions. A new commission needs a new RON notice. IPEN combines electronic records with physical appearance and follows its separate application process. The current FAQ lists a twenty-five-dollar RON maximum and a ten-dollar IPEN maximum. Ordinary video conferencing alone does not establish compliant RON.

sections.heading: Verify people and preserve usable evidence
sections.body: OAR 160-100-0805 requires credential analysis and human visual comparison with the live signer. Under its KBA procedure, five data-source multiple-choice questions have at least five choices each, with eighty percent correct within two minutes. Retakes have prescribed limits and replacement questions, and a signer exiting the act restarts the workflow. OAR 160-100-0855 requires tamper-evident electronic documents, privacy, clear synchronous communication and secure records. Preserve the person-to-person recording, associate it with the electronic journal and maintain accessible playback. Transaction documents are excluded from the video itself. The current FAQ separately requires the electronic RON journal.

example.heading: A dropped session after identity proofing
example.body: A Medford RON notary has completed platform identity checks when the signer exits the act and returns later. The notary restarts credential analysis and KBA under OAR 160-100-0805(5). A prior success screen and payment receipt do not replace the required restart. Once the actual session is completed lawfully, the recording and electronic journal are preserved through the relevant ten-year retention rules.

keyFacts: RON and IPEN have separate authorization processes.
The Oregon notary remains physically in Oregon.
The customer's KBA quiz is an identity process, not the licensing examination.
A recording supplements the required electronic RON journal.

articles.keyword: Oregon acknowledgments when the signature is already on the page
articles.title: Oregon acknowledgments when the signature is already on the page
articles.description: Work through earlier signatures, present appearances, certificate dates and representative capacity.
articles.h1: Oregon acknowledgments when the signature is already on the page
articles.lede: A signature made yesterday can support an acknowledgment today when the actual participant completes the required procedure.

sections.heading: Separate the two events
sections.body: At a Salem office, a seller brings a deed signed before leaving home. The Oregon guide permits a signature made before an acknowledgment. The notary still identifies the appearing person and obtains acknowledgment of willing execution. The earlier ink on the page does not establish that the notarial event has already occurred.

sections.heading: Date the act that happens
sections.body: The certificate describes the acknowledgment performed at the appointment. Its date should therefore identify that event. Backdating to the document signature would make the certificate describe the wrong time. The journal also distinguishes the document date from the date and time of the notarial act, preserving the actual sequence for later review.

sections.heading: Use the appropriate execution role
sections.body: If a company officer appears for the seller entity, the representative acknowledgment addresses authority and execution for that represented entity. The guide recommends suitable confirmation of the claimed representative capacity. The notary identifies the individual who appears and accurately records the representative role, without guaranteeing the company's debts or the transaction's financial merits.

sections.heading: Recognize a different requested act
sections.body: A document bearing a jurat or signature-witnessing certificate needs its own procedure. For those acts the guide requires present signing, and a jurat also requires the oath or affirmation. Ask the customer to resolve a mismatch between the requested act and printed certificate. A nonattorney notary should explain procedures neutrally and leave legal selection with the customer or adviser.

faqs.q: Can an acknowledgment cover yesterday's signature?
faqs.a: Yes. The signer must appear and acknowledge the earlier execution through the proper procedure.

faqs.q: Should its date match the document's date?
faqs.a: Use the actual acknowledgment date. The underlying signature and notarial event may have different dates.

articles.keyword: Building an Oregon credible-witness identification record
articles.title: Building an Oregon credible-witness identification record
articles.description: Check the witness relationship, sworn testimony, identity evidence and supporting journal information.
articles.h1: Building an Oregon credible-witness identification record
articles.lede: A credible witness supplies a particular identification link. The procedure still requires careful examination of both people's roles.

sections.heading: Identify the relationship being proved
sections.body: At a community office in Bend, an unfamiliar signer brings a friend who has known the signer for years. The witness must personally know the person being identified. A witness who merely knows the notary cannot supply that missing relationship. The Oregon guide also describes the witness as honest, competent and impartial.

sections.heading: Identify the witness too
sections.body: The notary may personally know the witness or satisfactorily identify that witness through an approved credential. These are separate links in the chain. The witness's willingness to help is not proof of the witness's identity, and a customer introduction does not automatically become the notary's own personal knowledge of either person. If the witness presents a damaged credential whose photograph cannot be compared reliably, the notary should resolve that uncertainty through additional satisfactory evidence before relying on the witness. The witness route does not bypass scrutiny of an unclear identification document.

sections.heading: Obtain the actual sworn testimony
sections.body: The witness makes an oath or affirmation identifying the signer under the guide's procedure. An unsworn letter or a casual assurance leaves that part unfinished. The guide's sample also addresses financial interest and party status. Neither an additional fee nor a second signature turns an interested party into an impartial credible witness.

sections.heading: Make the record intelligible
sections.body: The guide describes an entry for the witness and an entry for the signer's notarized document, with the witness identified as the signer's identification basis. Preserve the actual information and obtain the relevant signatures. The witness oath is part of identification and does not receive a separate notarial-act charge under the guide.

faqs.q: Must the notary have known the witness before the appointment?
faqs.a: No. The guide also permits identifying the witness through satisfactory approved identification.

faqs.q: Does the witness replace the signer's participation?
faqs.a: No. In the ordinary paper procedure, both witness and signer participate in person.

articles.keyword: Using Oregon journal shortcuts without losing the act record
articles.title: Using Oregon journal shortcuts without losing the act record
articles.description: Apply duplicate-original, multiple-document and previous-entry rules while preserving the actual events.
articles.h1: Using Oregon journal shortcuts without losing the act record
articles.lede: Oregon permits specific recordkeeping efficiencies. Each depends on facts that should remain visible in the journal.

sections.heading: Begin with contemporaneous recording
sections.body: An Eugene notary has several documents ready for one customer. The first requirement is to record the actual service at the time of the notarization. Pre-filling a completed-event account or asking the signer to return days later for the required journal signature would defeat that timing, regardless of how efficient the planned shortcut looks.

sections.heading: Recognize true duplicate originals
sections.body: When the same person signs duplicate originals on the same date, the guide allows one entry stating the number of originals notarized. This is a description of multiple performed acts. Simply omitting the number would hide the service volume. Text similarity also does not justify treating different dates or different people as one event.

sections.heading: Describe distinct same-day documents
sections.body: The guide separately permits one same-day entry for different statements or documents from the same signer when the distinct acts, document dates and document types are indicated. Another method uses separate lines with ditto marks for information genuinely repeated. Facts that differ must still be recorded accurately, including the nature of the distinct documents.

sections.heading: Keep a later visit distinct
sections.body: For a signer returning on a different date, the guide permits reference to previous entries for the address and identification description. That limited reference does not move the later act back to the earlier date or eliminate its record. Make the earlier entry easy to locate, and record the actual current procedure and fee or no-charge notation.

faqs.q: Can every repeated customer reuse an old entry?
faqs.a: The guide permits limited prior references for address and identification information. A new act still needs its record.

faqs.q: Does one entry mean only one act fee?
faqs.a: Journal-entry grouping and fee calculation have different purposes. Apply the appropriate fee rule to the acts actually performed.

articles.keyword: Oregon journal agreements when an employee changes jobs
articles.title: Oregon journal agreements when an employee changes jobs
articles.description: Plan workplace record custody, individual journals, retention and the stamp at departure.
articles.h1: Oregon journal agreements when an employee changes jobs
articles.lede: A signed journal agreement can change who retains a workplace journal. The official stamp remains under the notary's control.

sections.heading: Discuss custody before departure
sections.body: A Portland office buys journals and stamps for its employee notaries. Payment makes the tools convenient for the business, but the Oregon guide treats them as the individual notary's tools. If the employer expects to retain a workplace journal after departure, the guide calls for a signed journal agreement that addresses that retention.

sections.heading: Preserve the written arrangement
sections.body: When the agreement applies, the notary hands the covered journal to the employer and retains a copy of the agreement. That copy may be examined by the Secretary of State. Separate workplace and personal journals can make the agreed scope easier to administer when the notary also serves private customers outside the employment relationship.

sections.heading: Keep the continuing duties
sections.body: The employer retaining the journal follows the same retention and disclosure rules that otherwise apply to the notary. The guide gives a ten-year minimum measured from the last act in the journal. An agreement does not make entries suitable for unrestricted browsing, and it does not permit several notaries to merge their acts into a single office journal. During a permitted inspection, unrelated entries should remain concealed. An employer retaining a workplace journal should plan that controlled access as carefully as physical storage, because possession of the book does not turn every signer's address or signature into general business marketing information.

sections.heading: Take the stamp with the notary
sections.body: The stamp remains the notary's exclusive tool even when the business paid for it and a journal agreement exists. The business cannot give it to a successor employee. If the commission expires or the notary resigns, follow the disabling instructions. A change of employer should also prompt review of the commission contact record.

faqs.q: Does employer payment alone create journal-retention rights?
faqs.a: The guide requires the applicable signed journal agreement for employer retention on departure.

faqs.q: Can that agreement transfer the stamp too?
faqs.a: No. The guide requires the official stamp to remain with the notary.

articles.keyword: Oregon copy certification and the official-custodian boundary
articles.title: Oregon copy certification and the official-custodian boundary
articles.description: Distinguish copy fidelity, incomplete reproductions and public records needing custodian-certified copies.
articles.h1: Oregon copy certification and the official-custodian boundary
articles.lede: Copy certification starts by determining exactly which record is being reproduced and whether the requested act is permitted.

sections.heading: Determine the copying task
sections.body: A Corvallis customer needs a copy of a private letter for a distant recipient. Under the Oregon guide, the notary determines whether the reproduction is full, true and accurate. The notary should make or carefully oversee the copying. The certificate concerns the reproduction's fidelity and does not guarantee the truth of the writer's statements.

sections.heading: Check the whole reproduction
sections.body: A cropped margin, missing reverse side or omitted page can defeat a full and accurate copy. Compare what was actually supplied and reproduced. The guide even allows a copy of a copy when the certificate does not falsely claim an original was used. Truthful wording should identify the actual source and avoid overstating what the notary examined.

sections.heading: Use the custodian for public records
sections.body: Public records such as filed articles of incorporation have official custodians who supply certified copies. The guide also identifies specific restrictions for Oregon vital records, including birth and death certificates. A privately printed copy with a notary stamp does not become the issuing agency's certified record. Direct the requester to the proper record-holding office.

sections.heading: Keep appearance and warnings in view
sections.body: The guide requires the person requesting the certified copy to appear. It also advises checking Do Not Copy warnings and agency restrictions for proposed reproductions. A photograph by itself is not a notarizable statement under the guide, though an appropriate signed statement about a photograph may receive the selected notarial act.

faqs.q: Does copy certification prove that a letter's claims are true?
faqs.a: No. The notary determines the fidelity of the copy to the source.

faqs.q: Can a copy be made from a photocopy?
faqs.a: The guide permits it when the certificate accurately describes the source and does not falsely claim an original.

articles.keyword: Repairing an Oregon certificate after the customer leaves
articles.title: Repairing an Oregon certificate after the customer leaves
articles.description: Use verified facts, personal corrections and journal notes to preserve the relationship between certificate and record.
articles.h1: Repairing an Oregon certificate after the customer leaves
articles.lede: A correction should improve the evidence of the actual act while preserving a clear account of what changed.

sections.heading: Locate the factual error
sections.body: At a Grants Pass office, a recipient reports that a certificate names the wrong county. The notary first identifies the actual record and act and checks the journal. The Oregon guide requires support from the journal or the signer before correcting a completed certificate. The recipient's preferred wording alone does not establish historical facts.

sections.heading: Bring the actual record back
sections.body: The guide directs that the document return for the proper correction procedure. The notary should not send a detached completed certificate for someone else to attach. Keeping the correction with the identified record reduces the risk of a signed certificate being paired with a different document or used to describe an event that never occurred.

sections.heading: Make the correction personally
sections.body: Only the notary who completed the certificate should make its corrections. The guide describes drawing a line through incorrect information, placing the correction above it and initialing and dating nearby. It warns against white-out. If a stamp impression was smeared, reapply a clear impression. A helpful office assistant does not assume the notary's correction role.

sections.heading: Leave a supporting record
sections.body: Record the change in the journal so a later reviewer can understand the repair. Distinguish correction of supported certificate particulars from inventing a new appearance or changing an act type to achieve a legal outcome. If the requested correction cannot be verified, do not guess. The journal's value comes from preserving what actually occurred.

faqs.q: Can the document recipient fix the notary's certificate?
faqs.a: The guide requires the notary to make the correction personally.

faqs.q: What if the journal cannot confirm the requested date?
faqs.a: Seek verifiable support from the signer. The guide says not to make an unsupported correction.

articles.keyword: Quoting Oregon notarial fees with clear travel and waiver terms
articles.title: Quoting Oregon notarial fees with clear travel and waiver terms
articles.description: Identify the act category, give advance prices and maintain an accurate fee record.
articles.h1: Quoting Oregon notarial fees with clear travel and waiver terms
articles.lede: A clear quote identifies the actual notarial service and makes additional travel charges understandable before the appointment.

sections.heading: Identify the correct service category
sections.body: A mobile notary in Astoria offers ordinary paper acts, IPEN and approved RON. The guide gives a ten-dollar ordinary-act ceiling, and the current electronic FAQ applies that same maximum to IPEN. The RON maximum is twenty-five dollars. Using an electronic document at the same desk does not by itself make the appointment RON.

sections.heading: Count the services actually performed
sections.body: The guide explains that two people whose signatures are separately notarized can represent two acts even when they share a certificate. Journal shortcuts serve recordkeeping and do not redefine that fee unit. The credible witness oath used solely as the identification procedure is treated differently by the guide and does not receive a separate act charge.

sections.heading: Disclose additional travel in advance
sections.body: The ordinary fee schedule should be displayed or handed to the customer before notarization. Travel information belongs in that disclosure, and the travel amount must be agreed upon before meeting the customer. A surprise line item after arrival does not produce advance agreement. Whether the business retains collected act fees does not enlarge the permissible maximum. For example, a client who agrees to an ordinary acknowledgment price in a telephone conversation has not necessarily agreed to an undisclosed drive across the county. Resolve the separate travel amount before the trip, and keep the act-fee calculation within its own statutory category.

sections.heading: Check whether a waiver is on file
sections.body: A notary without a filed waiver can choose a free act. A filed waiver instead prevents charging until rescinded through the state process. The guide says it also follows the notary's after-hours work. Make the journal reflect the actual collected fee or a no-charge notation. Never record a maximum charge as collected when it was waived.

faqs.q: Does one certificate always mean one fee?
faqs.a: No. The guide's two-signer example counts the separate notarized signatures as acts.

faqs.q: Does an employer change cancel a fee waiver?
faqs.a: No. Follow the state rescission process before resuming charges under a filed waiver.

articles.keyword: Oregon foreign-language documents and professional boundaries
articles.title: Oregon foreign-language documents and professional boundaries
articles.description: Assess readable certificates, truthful participation and the limits of translation-related notarization.
articles.h1: Oregon foreign-language documents and professional boundaries
articles.lede: Language questions can affect identity, certificate understanding and the signer's ability to make the requested statement.

sections.heading: Understand what the certificate says
sections.body: A bilingual customer brings a document to a Hood River office. The guide allows a foreign-language certificate when the notary can read and write that language and the certificate meets Oregon requirements. The office title remains Notary Public in English. A notary who cannot understand the certificate should not certify unknown statements merely because the customer is confident.

sections.heading: Evaluate the document carefully
sections.body: The guide explains reasonable-care problems when the notary cannot read the document, including difficulty detecting blanks, identifying relevant names and recognizing inappropriate instructions. It recommends referral to a bilingual notary when needed. The notary should distinguish that guidance from a claim that every foreign-language document is automatically prohibited by a categorical Oregon statute.

sections.heading: Keep translation claims with their speaker
sections.body: A translator may provide a signed statement about accuracy for the appropriate notarial act. The translator makes that statement and any required oath or affirmation. The notary does not acquire expertise in the translated language simply by notarizing the signature. The requester should confirm whether the receiving agency accepts the proposed notarized translation and attached-certificate format.

sections.heading: Describe the office honestly
sections.body: Oregon restricts nonattorney use of notario or notario publico because those terms can convey legal-professional authority. The required advertising warning uses the advertisement's language and applies across media. The commission does not authorize choosing immigration petitions or drafting legal records. A customer's gratitude or willingness to pay does not expand that professional scope.

faqs.q: Can an Oregon certificate be in another language?
faqs.a: The guide permits it when the notary understands the language and it satisfies Oregon certificate requirements.

faqs.q: Does notarizing a translator's statement guarantee foreign acceptance?
faqs.a: No. The requester should confirm the receiving agency's requirements.

articles.keyword: Handling Oregon RON identity failures and session exits
articles.title: Handling Oregon RON identity failures and session exits
articles.description: Apply credential comparison, KBA limits and restart rules to a remote signing session.
articles.h1: Handling Oregon RON identity failures and session exits
articles.lede: Identity proofing is a workflow with failure conditions. A successful screen does not remove the notary's live review responsibilities.

sections.heading: Check the credential and the person
sections.body: In an approved RON session, a Medford notary receives an authenticity result for the signer's credential. OAR 160-100-0805 still requires a human comparison between the identification image and the person appearing live. If the notary cannot validate the credential or match the physical features, the rule prohibits completing the act.

sections.heading: Require usable images and present possession
sections.body: The rule requires captured images adequate for credential analysis and visual inspection, with legible text and clear relevant features. The notary confirms that the signer possesses the identification at the act and that the submitted images match that credential without manipulation. A saved image found in an old email is not automatic proof of present possession.

sections.heading: Keep the identity quiz within its rules
sections.body: The KBA procedure in the rule uses five multiple-choice questions drawn from data sources, with at least five choices per question. The signer must answer eighty percent correctly within two minutes. After first failure, the rule permits up to two additional quizzes within forty-eight hours and requires replacement of at least forty percent of prior questions on a retake.

sections.heading: Restart when the signer exits
sections.body: If the signer exits the notarial act, subsection (5) requires restarting credential analysis and KBA from the beginning. A prior identity success, uploaded image or payment receipt does not replace that restart. These KBA numbers describe remote identity authentication. They should never be presented as the specifications of Oregon's ordinary licensing examination.

faqs.q: May the notary ignore a face mismatch after automated approval?
faqs.a: No. The rule retains human comparison and prohibits completion when identity cannot be validated or matched.

faqs.q: How many old quiz questions must change on a five-question retake?
faqs.a: At least two questions, meeting the rule's forty-percent replacement requirement.

articles.keyword: Preserving Oregon RON recordings and electronic journals
articles.title: Preserving Oregon RON recordings and electronic journals
articles.description: Plan linked records, secure retention, reliable playback and vendor responsibilities.
articles.h1: Preserving Oregon RON recordings and electronic journals
articles.lede: Remote evidence is useful only when the correct interaction and journal record remain accessible for the applicable retention period.

sections.heading: Preserve two related records
sections.body: The current Oregon FAQ requires an electronic journal for RON, normally supplied by the vendor, including the signer's electronic signature. OAR 160-100-0855 separately addresses the audiovisual recording. The recording captures the person-to-person interaction and is logically associated with the electronic journal. Keeping one does not automatically satisfy the obligation to keep the other.

sections.heading: Separate documents from recorded interaction
sections.body: The technology rule requires completed RON documents to be electronically signed and rendered tamper-evident. It also says transaction documents must not be recorded as part of the video recording. A platform should therefore manage executed records and the recorded ceremony in the ways required for each, without substituting a screen video of documents for the personal interaction.

sections.heading: Use the correct retention reference points
sections.body: The FAQ measures electronic-journal retention as ten years from the journal's last transaction. The technology rule requires safe, secure RON records for ten years following the notarization and availability to the Secretary of State on request. A subscription ending, a new employer or a new ordinary commission does not automatically terminate these continuing record obligations.

sections.heading: Choose an archive that can be used
sections.body: The rule calls for recordings viewable and audible through broadly available players. A vendor contract should make retention responsibility clear before the notary begins using the platform. Plan for usable exports or continuing access when services change. A file locked behind discontinued proprietary hardware may remain on a disk yet fail the rule's playback standard.

faqs.q: Can the notary rely only on a video file?
faqs.a: No. RON also requires the electronic journal, with the recording properly associated to it.

faqs.q: Does canceling the vendor contract end retention?
faqs.a: No. Arrange continued compliant access and preservation for the required periods.
